notes.text: To every agent: while he is playing, BATCH your pushes. nangijala-deploy.yml triggers on games2/** and on every art domain, so any push - art, server or browser code - rolls a new Cloud Run revision and drops his socket. Measured tonight 17:49-18:07: six rollouts in eighteen minutes (4457-4460 monsters, 4461-4462 games-assistant). Each one restarts his world and re-streams everything on screen, and a client that loses one art request in that window keeps the hole until he restarts the app.

TONIGHT'S THREE LESSONS, all of them paid for by his evening. (1) NEVER push a board commit straight after a code commit: nangijala-deploy's `resolve` job skips a commit that is no longer main's head, and coordination/** triggers no deploy of its own, so the code silently never ships. Three of my pushes tonight never reached production, including one I told him was live. Code first, board only once the deploy run has left `resolve`. (2) A PUSH IS A WORLD RESTART for every agent: the deploy fires on games2/** AND every art domain. 17:49-18:07 ran SIX rollouts in eighteen minutes (4457-4460 monsters, 4461-4462 mine). Batch them while he plays. (3) MEASURE THE COST, NOT ONLY THE WIN. I cut ghost latency 416ms->52ms and never measured server CPU; EDGE_TICKS 2->1 plus a neighbour-wake rule made every room publish to every neighbour every tick, a world-scaled cost bought for a one-player benefit. Production then sat at 56-70% CPU with ZERO clients and stalled the event loop to 1.9s, which starved the SAME process's art serving and broke his game far worse than the boundary ever looked. Reverted in bbece9ba6c. NOTE for whoever takes the boundary next: the revert only halved the loop lag - ~56% CPU with nobody connected PREDATES tonight, and the standing suspicion is that one Node process running the authoritative 20Hz world should not also be serving ~50,000 art files.

ARTIFACT REGISTRY WAS 488 GB AND NOTHING HAD EVER DELETED AN IMAGE. Measured on his phone 2026-09-22 19:10: 'Repository Size: 488148.057MB'. Commit d54928100b measured 285 GB on 2026-08-15, so it grew +203 GB in 38 days = 5.3 GB/day. His billing export for 1-21 Sep: Cloud Run kr 240.81 list / kr 191.16 net (-17%, the fast lane working), Artifact Registry kr 181.73 (+41%) - the ONLY growing line, on course to pass Cloud Run and reach ~kr 509/month on its own within three months. Deriving from his own bill, the effective rate is ~kr 0.62/GB/mo. games2/deploy/ar-cleanup.sh existed since 2026-08-15 and had NEVER ONCE RUN: a fresh Cloud Shell opens as '(no project)', so DEVSHELL_PROJECT_ID and `gcloud config get-value` are both empty and the documented one-liner died on its first line - and its error told him to do something impossible (the paste PIPES the script, so there is no local file to name, and a PROJECT_ID=x prefix binds to curl, not to the bash across the pipe). NOTE ecf1fb9562, 2026-08-15, 'make the AR cleanup paste actually work from a phone': someone had ALREADY fixed this once, declared it fixed, and never ran it on a real phone. THE RULE: an ops paste is not fixed until it has been EXECUTED end to end by the person who has to run it - a script nobody can run is worth exactly nothing, and this one cost ~kr 126/month of standing spend plus ~kr 99/month more every month it continued. Fixed in 26be6eb3e3 (derives the project from `gcloud projects list`: one project is taken automatically, several hand back a ready line); both branches exercised against a stubbed gcloud before commit. The policy is now APPLIED server-side (keep newest 15, delete >14 days, dry-run off) and sweeps within 24h. Expected residual 10-25 GB, i.e. ~kr 10-20/month against ~kr 260 - and it needs CONFIRMING: re-read the size in 48h before anyone quotes the saving as fact.

FINDING 1 — RUNNING BREAKS A PHOTO TURN, BY DESIGN. Movement is not blocked mid-turn (only taps are swallowed) and the camera follows the body; the orbit's pivot is fixed at the tap and B is a photo taken at the swap. FINDING 2 — A COLD SIDE IS A FILL RATE, NOT A COMPOSE COST. His beacon (live/telemetry/perf.json, composeWorkerMs/composeLanded and composeApplyMs/composeLanded, builds c0efbebe66, a038861c46, 67fd594d4d): one transition = 0.37-0.51 ms on the compose worker + 0.08-0.09 ms main-thread upload. Plus ~83 art files only the new side shows (slopes, wall faces, scenery facings) not yet loaded at the tap.

FINDING 3 — THE CHECKERBOARD'S CAUSE. The round's banded paint (groundPaintSteps) went through the compose worker (boundary()/fade()/postPlate() post and return null => plain plate, cell owed), and viewSettled() checks t3stale, t3dropOwed, opsForCell textures, occIncomplete, sceneryAsked — NOT t3boundaryOwed / t3deckOwed — and B was also taken at the waitB timeout. B = plain diamonds. Rule for any future turn: never take B (or go live) while an owed boundary/deck cell meets the view rect or tex.inflightCount() > 0 for its keys. withoutComposeBudget does nothing while the worker is on.

FINDING 4 — WHAT THE REVERTED ROUND MEASURED (this machine, ~3-6x faster than his phone): swap of a kept view 350-600 ms in one block -> 44-62 ms over 7-8 frames (worst frame 7.6-12.6 ms); a first visit 430-580 -> 250-330 ms over 19-22 frames; night maps kept per view (viewKeep) 95-200 -> 3-11 ms; slope runs + ramp masks = 56-70 ms of a first visit (two whole-world passes, now kept per world + warmRamps); the world.json fetch once in idle time (a first tap waited 8.5 s for it on a busy harness); a driven turn's B check 3x60 ms was 180 ms of waiting on a view already drawn. On his phone a full repaintWorld frame = 52.9 ms; a full rebuildOccluders was 50-133 ms.

FINDING 5 — THE GPU TRANSITION COMPOSITOR. 25f3618cd0 (Sept 4) made a composition go to the GPU as raw bytes (6-9.6 ms -> ~0.09 ms of main thread each); composeworker (Sept 12) moved the blend off the frame thread — both are in. The GPU compositor itself (shader test d325e28fff/87818b0005) was REJECTED and removed in 2d2e63cc3b: 44-117 lag frames a window vs 7-15, but every run was confounded by monster-strip uploads (fixed hours later by the art queue), it drew ONE DRAW WITH PER-DRAW UNIFORMS PER BOUNDARY (Mali-hostile), and was 0.83% off the CPU composer. For turning it is the right tool: a boundary is a mask select between two plates that are already textures (+ the pattern sheet), so no side would ever owe a composition. Worth a re-test as ONE batched draw (per-vertex attributes / atlas, never per-draw uniforms), with a parity gate.

THE PLAN HE WAS SHOWN (his call which to build; he asked the questions, not for a revert of the plan):
FIX 1 — ALL FOUR SIDES READY BEFORE THE TAP. (a) once per side per session, in idle slices: rotated World + terrain grid + deck index + Tiles3World + the worker's resolver per orientation + night maps — this is the reverted 51090f1eda / f6ed5df6a3 code (viewCache, t3ViewCache, viewKeep, warmRamps, runSliced/swapSteps), recoverable from history; ~1 s of his CPU per side, once. (b) while moving, spare-time only, lowest priority: a ring per neighbour side (the far side last) — resolve its cells, post its transitions to the compose worker, fetch the art only it shows. Estimated on his phone: +1-2 ms/frame main thread (the `prefetch` section is 0.44-0.79 ms/frame for ONE side), +2-4% of a worker core, ~+20 MB GPU (~800 x 12 KB per side), nothing standing still; the resolution could go to the resolve worker (ml-resolve-worker, off by default). With the GPU compositor (finding 5) (b) shrinks to art + resolution. (c) at the tap: paint from ready parts + occluders/scenery, sliced over the first half of the turn under frame A (camera off there, so the time is free).
FIX 2 — A LIVE TURN, NOT A MOVIE. Move rotfx into Phaser's own GL context (a PostFXPipeline on the main camera, or an Extern; the repo already runs custom pipelines, e.g. SceneryLitPipeline). Captures become GPU copies (no texImage2D of a WebGL canvas across contexts, no owner-map readPixels — both stall a phone). From mid-turn the orbit samples the LIVE render of side B, figures as cards cut per frame on the GPU (owner map rendered, never read back), the pivot follows the live camera, and the last frame IS the live frame, so there is nothing to fade. The ground RT (world-anchored, bodiless, 512 px past every edge) can fill what neither frame saw instead of the dim soft fill.
ALTERNATIVE (taste): with Fix 1 in, an instant turn under a ~150 ms live motion-blur whip — cheapest, glitch-free by construction, loses the orbit.
